context: Session record. The snapshots design serializes every metadata writer (the start, the housekeeper delete, the restore) with one lease object in the bucket, and leaves open how the lease of a crashed writer ends. Options shown to the operator: A) a lease with an expiry, B) no lease, each record write is already a compare and swap, C) a lease with no expiry. The operator answered on 2026-10-28 in grill-phase2-03.md item 4: "A", and in grill-adr-phase2.md item 2: "I want to be prepare to the delete algo impl" (the housekeeper delete holds the lease for a whole run). On 2026-10-29 in decide-lease-60s.md item 1 the operator set the lease time: "let's reduce lease to 60s", with no reason given. Items 2 and 3, answer A: a clock margin of 30 seconds on each side and a renew every 10 seconds; neither value is measured. The operator also said in chat on 2026-10-29: "don't make lease a public interface". Implementation: a private helper takes, renews, and releases the lease; each write calls a check that returns an internal lease-lost error; a random token recognizes a lease write whose reply was lost. A crash blocks metadata writes for up to 90 seconds.

Session record. The DB of an instance and the instance record in the bucket both name the generation and the family of the instance. After a dump is restored, the two can disagree, and a start that writes then puts new data into a generation that the DB does not know. Options: A) check at every start and fail with no write, B) repair the mismatch at start, C) no startup change. The operator answered "A + B" for the bucket side and the instance-record part on 2026-10-28 (grill-phase2-03.md item 1); the snapshots design rejects a repair because it writes into a generation that the DB does not know. On a start whose metadata storage cannot open, the operator chose "B" in chat on 2026-10-28: the start fails, over skipping the metadata or a feature flag. On 2026-10-30 in chat the operator said "2 keys": the DB keeps the generation and the family as two keys in its instance metadata table. Implementation: the check runs right after the instance id exists; the storage opens before the core init; a DB backup skips both keys by name.

Session record. Records are YAML documents in the bucket that tools with no backend read, and later parts of the design add fields to them; an older housekeeper must still read a newer record. In the TODO-8 review on 2026-10-28 (grill-todo8-comments.md) the operator said "add version to all yaml entities"; the recommendation not to refuse a newer version was accepted with no comment. Rejected: strict decoding that refuses an unknown field; refusing a version above the one the reader knows. Implementation: each record has an UnmarshalYAML method that checks the fields of its phase; the version is an integer first key; the library is gopkg.in/yaml.v3.

Session record. Users of the deploy CLI want to see what a deploy would change before it changes anything. Options: A) a --dry-run flag that prints every create, update, and delete and applies none, B) a separate plan command that writes a plan file, C) no preview. The operator chose A in chat on 2026-09-12: "a flag is enough, a plan file is one more thing to lose". The preview must exit non-zero when the real deploy would fail. Implementation: the flag swaps the cloud client for a recording client and prints its log at the end. This is a feature: what the user can do and see.
